verdict.summary: Nebius has the strongest operating momentum among the neocloud cohort, but its valuation and financing cadence assume that exceptional Q2 unit economics survive a brutal capacity ramp. Q2 2026 revenue rose 454% to $582.3 million; AI cloud supplied $574.9 million, or 98% of group revenue, and the segment delivered a 50% adjusted EBITDA margin. Annualized run-rate revenue reached $3.0 billion, while management reported more than $9 billion of expected 2026 customer prepayments. The June 30 legal denominator is 271.855 million Class A plus Class B shares, not the 238.4 million Class A figure. At $209.7599, that implies about $57.03 billion of equity value and $59.19 billion of enterprise value after $10.20 billion debt and $8.04 billion cash, or roughly 43.5x trailing revenue and 229x EBITDA. Pre-funded warrants, awards and gross convert claims sit outside that legal count. The C+ grade recognizes growth and dilution. The unchanged $214.28 plan is rejected because TP1 offers only 1.23R.

whyAvoid: Point-in-time valuation is approximately 43.5x EV/TTM revenue and 229.4x EV/EBITDA on the rebuilt Class A-plus-Class B denominator.

The August 2026 financing plan contemplated $4.5B of new convertible notes.
AI cloud produces 98% of revenue, creating a concentrated economic engine despite multiple corporate assets.

business.overview:
Nebius sells GPU cloud capacity and an AI-native software platform, with AI cloud accounting for nearly all current group revenue. Sales are driven by deployed GPU clusters, customer utilization, contract pricing and the pace at which new capacity becomes available.

The AI transmission channel is direct: model builders and enterprises reserve accelerators, often prepaying to secure capacity; Nebius uses those commitments to finance GPUs and datacenters, then recognizes cloud revenue as service is delivered. Q2 annualized run-rate revenue of $3.0B and four billion-dollar-scale contracts demonstrate this loop.

The model breaks if GPU pricing compresses, customer prepayments reverse into delivery disputes, power or equipment arrives late, or capital raised through converts and equity fails to produce adequate returns. The broader group offers optionality, but 98% AI-cloud revenue means the current equity thesis is concentrated. The decisive evidence will be recognized revenue, deployed megawatts and cash payback after financing costs, not contract count or prepayment inflows viewed independently.
business.moat: Nebius combines GPU access, purpose-built datacenters, cloud software and unusually large customer prepayments. Its reported one-year-ten-month payback and Q2 ACV above $20M per MW suggest attractive current unit economics, but those economics are vulnerable to competition and falling compute prices.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 2026 group revenue was $582.3M, up 454% YoY and 46% sequentially. AI cloud revenue was $574.9M, up 514%, and its adjusted EBITDA margin reached 50%; those margin figures are non-GAAP. ARR was $3.0B, up 598% YoY, and cash was about $8B after $2.3B of positive operating cash flow that included customer prepayments. Management reaffirmed its 2026 guidance and outlook and expected more than $9B of customer prepayments. The caveat is conversion quality: prepayments create cash and deferred revenue before service delivery, so capacity commissioning and contract performance remain necessary before the economics are earned. No confirmed Nebius next-results date was announced in the official investor materials reviewed.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: At June 30 Nebius had 238,400,165 Class A and 33,455,053 Class B shares outstanding, or a 271,855,218-share legal denominator; Class C was nil. The 12,729,493 ATM shares sold at a $223.60 average were delivered from treasury and are included in that count, while 12,270,507 program shares remained unsold. Outside the legal count, 21,065,936 NVIDIA pre-funded warrants are treated as outstanding for EPS, 10,043,254 awards were anti-dilutive in Q2, and 65,416,804 gross if-converted shares were excluded from diluted EPS. Adding those observable claims yields a 368.4M sensitivity, not a fully diluted forecast, because convert settlement and capped calls can change actual issuance. At $209.7599, the legal count implies $57.03B market capitalization and approximately $59.19B enterprise value after $10.20B debt and $8.04B cash.

filingsReview.summary: 7 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade C+ measures fundamentals; trade state rejected measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The August 12 Form 6-K furnishes the Q2 release and shareholder letter: Q2 2026 group revenue was $582.3M and AI cloud revenue was $574.9M, versus $105.1M and $93.7M respectively in Q2 2025. It also supports ARR, contracted-power and customer-prepayment disclosures; it is an operating-results filing, not evidence of a completed securities sale.

The companion August 12 Form 6-K financial review supports the June 30 legal Class A and Class B counts, cash, debt, awards, pre-funded warrants and gross if-converted claims used in the basic-to-observable-dilution bridge; the 368.4M figure remains a sensitivity rather than a fixed fully diluted count.
The amended 2025 Form 20-F establishes Nebius's audited annual reporting and foreign-private-issuer risk baseline; it does not contain the later Q2 2026 revenue, ARR or prepayment KPIs.
The August 26 Form 6-K reports the decision-relevant financing update, including the proposed $4.5B convertible-note scale; it should not be used to source unrelated Q2 operating results.

The November 424B5 established a 25M-share at-the-market program. The later Q2 shareholder letter reports 12.7M shares sold at a $223.60 weighted average for about $2.8B gross and 12.3M shares remaining; capacity and completed sales are therefore separated.

The September 424B5 documents the completed 10,810,811-share common offering and the associated $2.75B convertible-note financing, which are distinct primary-equity and debt securities transactions. This classification controls the editorial conclusion.

This preliminary 424B5 offered 10,810,811 Class A shares and described concurrent $1.0B 2030 notes plus $1.0B 2032 notes, each with a $150M option. Final documents establish completion and prevent double-counting the later $2.75B note result.

contrarianRisks: The 25M-share ATM was partly used: 12.7M shares were sold by June 30 and 12.3M remained available.
The 10,810,811-share offering and $2.75B converts are separate financing components and should not be conflated.
The August 2026 6-K supports only the financing facts it contains, not unrelated operating claims.
Customer prepayments increase deferred revenue and delivery obligations even when they improve cash flow.
A foreign private issuer reports on the 20-F/6-K cadence rather than domestic 10-Q conventions.
